oil.summary: A deeply bifurcated session defined oil markets on 31 August. WTI surged +2.84% to $85.77/bbl, supported by acute Strait of Hormuz risk after Iranian state media confirmed a supertanker was struck by naval mines and Tehran vowed its oil blockade would continue until US-Israeli strikes cease. Brent, however, fell -1.27% to $88.21/bbl, likely weighed by a reported temporary US easing of Russian oil sanctions aimed at taming the price spike — a move that riled European allies. RBOB gasoline cratered -11.38%, a notable outlier that may reflect end-of-summer demand seasonality and switching in refined product flows. Heating oil continued its strong run, +1.43% on the day and +7.22% on the month. Middle East diesel exports to Africa have collapsed to nine-year lows with Asian suppliers stepping in. Russia's domestic refining capacity is now sufficiently degraded by Ukrainian strikes that Moscow is reportedly importing jet fuel for military operations.
drivers: Strait of Hormuz crisis escalates: supertanker mined, Iran maintains blockade threat, tanker traffic severely disrupted
US temporarily eases Russia oil sanctions to cap price surge, partially offsetting geopolitical premium in Brent
RBOB gasoline collapses -11.38% on the day, diverging sharply from crude; Middle East refined product flows to Africa at nine-year lows

gas.summary: European gas prices were the standout mover today, with TTF jumping +4.91% to 70.27 €/MWh — its highest level since 2023 according to published headlines — driven directly by re-escalating US-Iran hostilities intensifying Strait of Hormuz shipping fears and threatening LNG transit routes. Henry Hub was comparatively subdued, rising +1.28% to $2.925/MMBtu, continuing its one-month uptrend of +6.48%. On the demand side, China's LNG imports are tracking for an 18% year-on-year decline in August, breaking a three-month growth streak as high prices suppress purchasing. On the supply side, BP brought the Fayoum-4 well in Egypt's West Nile Delta onstream two years ahead of schedule, adding approximately 80 MMcf/d to regional supply.
drivers: TTF surges +4.91% to highest since 2023 as Iran-US conflict intensifies concerns over Strait of Hormuz LNG shipping
China's LNG imports set to fall ~18% year-on-year in August, reversing three months of growth as prices erode demand
BP starts Fayoum-4 well in Egypt two years early, adding ~80 MMcf/d to West Nile Delta supply

power.summary: EU Carbon EUAs edged down -0.57% to $78.155/EUA, effectively flat on a weekly and monthly basis, providing little directional signal on its own. The dominant macro backdrop for the power and carbon complex remains the Middle East conflict now six months old, with no clear resolution in sight according to today's reporting — sustaining elevated gas input costs that pressure power generators across Europe. TTF's +4.91% single-day move is the most consequential price input for European power dispatch economics today. Separately, SLB announced a $3.4 billion acquisition to expand into AI data center infrastructure, a signal of where oilfield services capital sees structural power demand growth. The UK Chancellor is reported to be weighing an expanded windfall tax on oil firms and banks amid sector profit surges. News flow on this sector is otherwise thin.
drivers: EU EUAs near flat at $78.16 while TTF's +4.91% spike squeezes European power generation margins via higher gas input costs
Six months of US-Iran conflict with no resolution raises persistent risk premium across energy inputs affecting power pricing
SLB commits $3.4 billion to AI data center infrastructure, underscoring structural growth in power demand from the technology sector
